runbook: R-18 / R-19 (fresh independent oracle; evidence tree = git archive HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md only)
what_the_leaf_means: Per data/worklists/f3-task.md, the 'derived order' is produced by src/calculator/rotation_resolver.py, which derives a cast order on the fly from the atomized ability data. Its first signal is automatic setup/consume-edge detection: 'an ability whose row names indicate application ... must precede abilities that consume ...'. rotation/setup[] is therefore the setup (producer) phase of the derived order, and setup[0] is the first ability that must be cast before its consumers. The trailing '60' matches the Syndra module's splinters option at the 60-Splinter threshold (W's Transcendent true-damage bonus), per data/champion-audit/batch-e9-1.json.

computation.step_1_identify_the_producer: In Syndra's kit exactly one ability creates the object every other ability consumes: Q 'Dark Sphere' — 'Syndra conjures a Dark Sphere at the target location ... The Dark Sphere then remains on the ground for 6 seconds.' (data/champions.json, Syndra.abilities.Q[0].effects[0].description)
step_2_identify_the_consumers: W 'Force of Will': 'Syndra telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere, enemy minion or non-epic monster within 500 units ...' and 'She prioritizes grabbing the nearest unit, then Dark Spheres.' — W's damage row (Recast: 'throws the grabbed target ... dealing magic damage') has no payload without a grabbable object.

E 'Scatter the Weak': 'Dark Spheres can be knocked back for 950 units ... Targets hit are also stunned for 1.25 seconds ...' — E's sphere/stun branch exists only if a Dark Sphere is already on the ground.

R 'Unleashed Power': 'Syndra conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones, ... each dealing magic damage upon hit.' The sourced rows are Minimum Magic Damage 240/360/480 (+60% AP) = 3 spheres and Maximum Magic Damage 560/840/1120 (+140% AP) = 7 spheres; reaching the maximum row requires 4 pre-existing spheres, i.e. prior Q casts.
computation.step_3_edge_direction: The detected setup/consume edges are Q -> {W, E, R}. There is no edge in the opposite direction: nothing in Syndra's cached rows consumes E's output. E applies a stun (and, at 80 Splinters, a slow), but no Syndra damage row is conditioned on a stunned/slowed target (no 'Enhanced', 'Bonus vs', 'per stack' or '% of target's' row keys off E). E is a consumer only.

step_4_dps_signal_(f3_rule_1b,_total_raw.sourced_inputs: Q rank5 230 (+70% AP), cd 7 at every rank (cooldown.affectedByCdr = false; R passive grants Dark Sphere 10/20/30 ability haste). W rank5 190 (+65% AP), cd 12/11/10/9/8, affectedByCdr = true; at 60 Splinters the Transcendent row applies, Total Mixed Damage rank5 = 212.8 (+76.6% AP). E rank5 200 (+60% AP), cd 15 at every rank, affectedByCdr = true.
step_4_dps_signal_(f3_rule_1b,_total_raw.formula: effective_cd = base_cd x 100/(100+AH) (docs/math-foundations.md, Section 5 audit table: 'Ability haste (effective_cooldown) | cd' = cd*100/(100+AH) | EXACT')
step_4_dps_signal_(f3_rule_1b,_total_raw.conclusion: E is strictly last on the DPS signal at every AP/AH point tested (its 15 s cooldown is more than double Q's and its damage is the lowest of the three). Q leads at low AP/AH; W overtakes Q only once the 60-Splinter true-damage bonus plus high AP is in play. Under no configuration does E rank first.

computation.step_5_verdict_reasoning: Both derivation signals put Q ahead of E. On the setup/consume signal Q is the sole producer and E is one of its consumers, so 'E' at setup[0] places a consumer before its producer — exactly the violation the F3 invariant suite forbids ('the derived order never violates a detected setup/consume edge'). On the DPS signal E is last, not first. The 60-Splinter state changes only W's damage (true-damage bonus) and Q's charges (40-Splinter threshold, already active); it creates no producer role for E. Therefore setup[0] = Q.

counter_hypothesis_considered: Real-game Syndra 'E-then-Q' tech exists (Q's sphere appears after a 0.6 s delay and the E notes say 'Spheres spawned at close range of the ability are more likely to be hit'), which could motivate casting E fractionally before Q. This is a cast-time/travel-window nuance, not a data-detectable atom edge, and it does not change the dependency: the sphere must still exist for the stun branch, and the sphere path adds no damage ('dealt Scatter the Weak's damage if they were not damaged by the initial cast' — no extra damage). It does not support E as the setup producer.
